reviews.reasoning: Re-derived every load-bearing claim. Ps 38 is a shift+1 psalm, so the title dual-cite web:Ps.38.0 = oshb:Ps.38.1 is arithmetically correct (ps_lib.web_to_mt(38,1) = (38,2)); the span's WEB verses 1-8 map to oshb:Ps.38.2-Ps.38.9. The title bytes at oshb:Ps.38.1 are 'מִזְמ֖וֹר לְדָוִ֣ד לְהַזְכִּֽיר' (collate tier byte), carrying exactly the three labels the row names. The lehazkir exclusivity claim holds on an independent skeleton sweep: 2 verses book-wide, MT Ps.38.1 and Ps.70.1 = web:Ps.38.0 and web:Ps.70.0, i.e. 2 psalms; psalm_device_inventory.json genre_label_membership lehazkir = [38, 70], so the attribution 'per the genre-label inventory' is accurate as well as byte-true. The vocative architecture checks out: a pointed scan of MT Ps.38.2-Ps.38.23 puts divine-name tokens in exactly 5 verses (MT 38:2, 38:10, 38:16, 38:22, 38:23 = web:Ps.38.1, 38:9, 38:15, 38:21, 38:22), so the next address after web:Ps.38.1 really is web:Ps.38.9 with nothing intervening in web:Ps.38.2-8. The arithmetic 8 of 22 WEB verses = 36% is correct (ps_lib.LAST_VERSE[38] = 22). WEB quotations at web:Ps.38.1 and web:Ps.38.8 are verbatim. Observation, not a defect: the span opens at web:Ps.38.1 while the title it cites is web:Ps.38.0, which is the settled title-citation form and tiles exactly (35/35 verses over Ps.38.1-Ps.39.13, no gaps or overlaps).

The seams are sound and I do not contest the span. The opening seam is carried by the vocative at MT 38:10 = web:Ps.38.9, and the closing seam by MT 38:16 = web:Ps.38.15, which opens 'כִּֽי לְךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה' (collate tier byte) — a ki-clause plus vocative, tier-1. The row's claim that no vocative recurs between web:Ps.38.9 and web:Ps.38.15 is confirmed by a pointed scan of the intervening bytes: 0 divine-name tokens across the 5 verses MT 38:11-38:15 = web:Ps.38.10-38:14. The deaf/mute self-description does end at web:Ps.38.14 (MT 38:15). The defect is confined to evidence bookkeeping in device_notes, below.

challenges.claim: device_notes argues 3 out-of-span verse ranges of Psalm 38 (16 verses) by bare 'vv.' mention, of which 15 verses are unmirrored in boundary_evidence_refs; the refs-mirror rule covers bare verse mentions resolved against the span psalm.
challenges.evidence: device_notes reads: 'The Ps 38 rows describe one bodily-affliction lament moving from wrath (vv. 1-8) through isolation and silence (vv. 9-14) to hope and enemies (vv. 15-20) and a closing plea (vv. 21-22).' The row's span is Ps.38.9-Ps.38.14, so web:Ps.38.1-8, web:Ps.38.15-20 and web:Ps.38.21-22 are argued outside the span — 16 verses. boundary_evidence_refs holds web:Ps.38.9, .11, .12, .13, .14, .15, of which web:Ps.38.15 is the single out-of-span entry: 16 out-of-span verses argued, 1 mirrored, 15 unmirrored (web:Ps.38.1-8 and web:Ps.38.16-22). The content of the summary is accurate (web:Ps.38.1 “Yahweh, don’t rebuke me in your wrath”; web:Ps.38.19 “But my enemies are vigorous and many”; web:Ps.38.21 “Don’t forsake me, Yahweh”), so this is a mirror defect, not a factual one — hence low. It is invisible to check_refs_mirror.py because its lesson-j arm uses VERSE_WORD = '\\bv(?:erse)?s?\\.?\\s+(\\d{1,3})(?:\\s*[-\u2013]\\s*(\\d{1,3}))?\\b', which cannot match the doubled 'vv.' form: findall('vv. 1-8') = [], findall('vv. 15-20') = [], while findall('verses 3-5') = [('3','5')]. Running the checker on this row returns argued-minus-covered-minus-span = [] (GREEN) purely because of that regex gap.

reviews.reasoning: The span is well founded and I do not contest it. Its opening is carried by MT 38:16 = web:Ps.38.15 ('כִּֽי לְךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה', collate tier byte), and a formal feature the row does not cite corroborates the unit: 4 consecutive verses, MT 38:16, 38:17, 38:18 and 38:19 (= web:Ps.38.15-38:18), open with the particle ki, and the next 2 verses, MT 38:20-38:21 (= web:Ps.38.19-38:20), open with waw plus noun, so the whole span coheres formally and the next volitive clause does not arrive until MT 38:22 = web:Ps.38.21. The claim that the next address break is 6 verses later is arithmetically right (web:Ps.38.15 to web:Ps.38.21) and the pointed scan confirms no divine-name token in MT 38:17-38:21 = web:Ps.38.16-38:20. The rejected_alternative names a real rival (splitting at web:Ps.38.18|web:Ps.38.19) and rebuts it on a ground that is true for that seam. One original-language mislabel stands, shared with the seam partner at web:Ps.38.21.

challenges.claim: The row calls web:Ps.38.21 an 'imperative cluster', but MT 38:22 contains no imperative — both of its volitive clauses are 'al plus a prefix-conjugation form (prohibitive), not imperatives.
challenges.evidence: web:Ps.38.21 = oshb:Ps.38.22 (Ps 38 is shift+1; ps_lib.web_to_mt(38,21) = (38,22)). The pointed bytes of the two clauses are 'אַל תַּֽעַזְבֵ֥נִי' and 'אַל תִּרְחַ֥ק' (both collate tier byte against oshb:Ps.38.22). Each is the negative particle 'al followed by a taw-prefixed prefix-conjugation form; Biblical Hebrew does not negate the imperative, and the imperative of these roots would carry no prefix consonant. The contrast is visible one verse later inside the same seam pair: MT 38:23 = web:Ps.38.22 opens 'ח֥וּשָׁה' (collate tier byte), a bare imperative with no prefix consonant. Both witnesses render the MT 38:22 pair as negative commands (web:Ps.38.21 “Don’t forsake me, Yahweh. My God, don’t be far from me”), which is consistent with prohibitive force but not with the label 'imperative'. Severity low: the row's warrant is a mood shift to direct command, and prohibitive volitives satisfy that warrant, so only the morphological label is wrong. Per seam-pair discipline this is one cure to be authored once and installed on both rows meeting at web:Ps.38.20|web:Ps.38.21 (see OL-107-1).

reviews.reasoning: I support the seam and the span: MT 38:22-38:23 = web:Ps.38.21-38:22 is a genuine two-verse close, marked by a shift to volitive address after the ki-chain and waw-pair of the preceding unit, and the arithmetic 'final 2 of 22 WEB verses' is right (ps_lib.LAST_VERSE[38] = 22). Both verses carry divine-name vocatives (MT 38:22 YHWH plus 'elohay, MT 38:23 'adonay), so the address density the row leans on is real. The rationale's central morphological claim is nevertheless wrong.

challenges.claim: 'A double imperative closes the psalm' and 'two imperatives (‘Don’t forsake’/‘Hurry to help’)' miscount the forms: only web:Ps.38.22 is an imperative, while web:Ps.38.21 carries two 'al-plus-prefix prohibitives.
challenges.evidence: web:Ps.38.21 = oshb:Ps.38.22 and web:Ps.38.22 = oshb:Ps.38.23 (shift+1). The row's first member is 'אַל תַּֽעַזְבֵ֥נִי' with its parallel 'אַל תִּרְחַ֥ק' (both collate tier byte against oshb:Ps.38.22): negative particle 'al plus taw-prefixed prefix-conjugation, the standard prohibitive, twice — so the verse the row counts as one imperative is in fact two non-imperative volitives. The second member 'ח֥וּשָׁה' (collate tier byte against oshb:Ps.38.23) is the 1 true imperative among the 3 volitive clauses in the span's 2 verses. The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so this is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses: WEB renders the pair as prohibitions (web:Ps.38.21 “Don’t forsake me, Yahweh. My God, don’t be far from me”) against a positive command at web:Ps.38.22 (“Hurry to help me, Lord, my salvation”). Low severity — the mood argument that drives the seam survives the correction, and the fix is the same single seam-pair edit as OL-106-1.

reviews.reasoning: This row's original-language work is byte-clean throughout, and it is right where the shared inventory is wrong. Both quoted runs collate at byte tier against oshb:Ps.39.1: ketiv 'לידיתון' and qere 'לִֽידוּת֗וּן', and the ketiv/qere assignment matches the staged form exactly (the unpointed ketiv precedes the pointed qere in the source bytes). The K/Q disclosure is warranted: pmarks_Ps.json kq carries 1 note at Ps.39.1. The dual-cite web:Ps.39.0 = oshb:Ps.39.1 is correct for a shift+1 psalm. The contrast drawn with Ps 62 and Ps 77 is byte-true: tokenising the maqaf-free skeletons of the 3 Jeduthun titles, 2 carry a standalone 'al token before the Jeduthun word (oshb:Ps.62.1, oshb:Ps.77.1) and 1 does not (oshb:Ps.39.1, which prefixes lamed instead) — so li-Yedutun versus al-Yedutun is exactly right. NOTE FOR THE TOOLKIT, not against the row: psalm_device_inventory.json files psalm 39 under genre_label_membership al_yeduthun = [39, 62, 77] and superscriptions['39'].labels = ['mizmor','lamnatseach','le_david','al_yeduthun']. That membership is the intended post-erratum widening (the label regex previously missed the prefixed form entirely), but the label NAME now misdescribes 1 of its 3 members: oshb:Ps.39.1 carries no 'al token at all. The two variables are orthogonal and the single label collapses them — preposition (lamed at Ps 39 versus 'al at Ps 62 and Ps 77) is independent of Jeduthun spelling (ketiv/qere pairs at Ps 39 and Ps 77, single spelling at Ps 62). A downstream row that read the label as its wording reads would assert 'al for Ps 39 against the bytes; this row declined to inherit it. The seam claims also hold: no divine-name token occurs in MT 39:2-39:4 = web:Ps.39.1-39.3, and web:Ps.39.3 does end “I spoke with my tongue:” with the colon introducing the address that opens at web:Ps.39.4. Observations only: the colon is an English rendering feature and carries corroborative weight at most, though the underlying MT 39:4 clause independently introduces speech; and the title summary omits lamnatseach, which the title also carries, without claiming to be exhaustive.

The selah arithmetic and disclosure are correct: pmarks_Ps.json selah lists exactly Ps.39.6 and Ps.39.12 for this psalm, so web:Ps.39.5 = oshb:Ps.39.6 is right, '1 of 2 selahs in this psalm' is right, and the row is properly disciplined in saying selah corroborates rather than drives. The adopted seam at web:Ps.39.6|web:Ps.39.7 is defensible and I do not ask for the span to be recut — MT 39:8 = web:Ps.39.7 opens with we-'attah plus the vocative 'adonay, a tier-1 pivot, and an 'ak chain straddles the rival seam ('אַךְ בְּצֶ֤לֶם' and 'אַךְ הֶ֥בֶל' at MT 39:7, both collate tier byte), which genuinely argues for keeping web:Ps.39.6 with what precedes it. My challenge is that the row never uses that argument and instead disposes of the rival on a warrant the rival does not rest on, while leaving the refrain member inside its own span undisclosed.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative substitutes a tier-3 warrant for the rival's tier-1 one: it frames the web:Ps.39.5 close as resting on Selah and rebuts that, when the rival's actual driver is a two-member refrain whose twin is treated as unit-closing at web:Ps.39.11, and the row never discloses that a refrain member sits inside its span.
challenges.evidence: The rejected_alternative reads: 'Ending the strophe at web:Ps.39.5, where Selah falls, is a live alternative; it is not adopted alone because Selah corroborates a close but does not itself drive one'. But a skeleton sweep of the refrain core returns 2 verses book-wide — MT Ps.39.6 and MT Ps.39.12 = web:Ps.39.5 and web:Ps.39.11 — i.e. a closed two-member lattice inside this psalm. The members are 'אַ֥ךְ כָּֽל הֶ֥בֶל כָּל אָ֝דָ֗ם נִצָּ֥ב סֶֽלָה' (oshb:Ps.39.6 = web:Ps.39.5) and 'אַ֤ךְ הֶ֖בֶל כָּל אָדָ֣ם סֶֽלָה' (oshb:Ps.39.12 = web:Ps.39.11), both collate tier byte, each opening with 'ak and closing with selah. That is inclusio/refrain structure, tier-1, not selah corroboration. The asymmetry is internal to the cluster: at web:Ps.39.11 the refrain member is span-final and is expressly called 'the return of the mortality refrain', while at web:Ps.39.5 the twin member is span-interior and is not identified as a refrain member anywhere in this row's rationale, device_notes or observed_substrate_signals. WEB corroborates the rival seam independently of selah: the speech block opened at web:Ps.39.4 closes at the end of web:Ps.39.5 (“Surely every man stands as a breath.” Selah.) and a new block opens at web:Ps.39.6 (“Surely every man walks like a shadow.). The cure is a re-cut rejected_alternative that meets the refrain warrant and an observed_substrate_signals entry disclosing the in-span refrain member; the span itself can stand on the 'ak chain at MT 39:7.

challenges.claim: device_notes carries a banned positional row reference.
challenges.evidence: device_notes reads: 'This psalm's earlier selah falls inside this span; the later one closes the next row (web:Ps.39.11).' 'the next row' is a positional row reference, which the standing register rule bans from row prose outright; cross-row references must be verse-anchored, e.g. 'the unit that closes at web:Ps.39.11'. The parenthetical verse anchor does not cure the positional phrasing. This is one seam-pair cure with OL-110-1, which carries the mirror-image phrase on the other side of the web:Ps.39.6|web:Ps.39.7 seam, and must be authored once and installed on both rows in the same pass.

reviews.reasoning: The span and its selah work are sound. web:Ps.39.11 = oshb:Ps.39.12 is correct arithmetic for a shift+1 psalm, '2 of 2 selahs in this psalm' matches pmarks_Ps.json exactly (Ps.39.6 and Ps.39.12 and no others), and the close is driven by the vocative opening MT 39:13 = web:Ps.39.12 ('שִֽׁמְעָ֥ה תְפִלָּתִ֨י יְהוָ֡ה', collate tier byte) with selah in a corroborating role only — the discipline the brief asks for. The opening seam at MT 39:8 = web:Ps.39.7 is a genuine we-'attah plus vocative pivot. Two defects, one register and one in the rival rebuttal.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative's ground — that no address marker interrupts the sequence between the vocatives at web:Ps.39.7 and web:Ps.39.12 — is either false or tautological, because two imperatives addressed to God stand inside that stretch and this cluster elsewhere treats an imperative cluster as an address break.
challenges.evidence: Inside the stretch, MT 39:9 = web:Ps.39.8 carries 'הַצִּילֵ֑נִי' and MT 39:11 = web:Ps.39.10 opens 'הָסֵ֣ר' (both collate tier byte), each a prefix-consonant-free imperative addressed to God; WEB renders them “Deliver me from all my transgressions” (web:Ps.39.8) and “Remove your scourge away from me” (web:Ps.39.10). If 'address marker' includes imperative address, the claim is false; if it means only a divine-name vocative, the sentence reduces to 'no vocative between the two vocatives' and carries no weight against the rival. The inconsistency is internal to the cluster: at web:Ps.38.21 an 'imperative cluster' is treated as precisely the address break that terminates a span, whereas here imperatives of the same class are not treated as markers at all. Low severity: the span is independently secured by the we-'attah pivot at MT 39:8 and the vocative at MT 39:13, so only the rebuttal's stated ground needs re-cutting to a criterion the cluster applies consistently.

reviews.reasoning: Verified end to end. The opening seam is tier-1 and strong: MT 39:13 = web:Ps.39.12 opens 'שִֽׁמְעָ֥ה תְפִלָּתִ֨י יְהוָ֡ה' (collate tier byte), imperative plus the divine-name vocative. The count claim is exact on the vocative reading — a pointed scan of MT Ps.39.1-39.14 puts divine-name tokens in exactly 3 verses, MT 39:5, 39:8 and 39:13 = web:Ps.39.4, 39:7 and 39:12 — so web:Ps.39.12 is indeed the third and last. 'Final 2 of 13 WEB verses' is correct (ps_lib.LAST_VERSE[39] = 13), and both WEB quotations are verbatim. WEB's own speech-block punctuation corroborates the span: the block opened at web:Ps.39.12 closes at the end of web:Ps.39.13, matching the row's boundaries exactly. Two observations that do not rise to challenges: 'direct address to God' is precise only if read as vocative address, since vocative-free imperatives address God at MT 39:9, 39:11 and 39:14 (= web:Ps.39.8, 39:10, 39:13), and the leading word 'vocative' in the same signal supplies that scoping; and the closing verse MT 39:14 = web:Ps.39.13 opens with an imperative, so the couplet is imperative-framed at both ends, which the row could cite but does not need to.
